newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London closed firmer following a stronger performance in New York. The March contract closed at $307.60, up $2.70, while May added $2.40 to close at $307.10. There was no fresh news to influence prices although Russia's Foreign Trade Ministry rejected market talk of bilateral negotiations with Cuba to buy 500,000 tonnes of sugar for second-quarter delivery.

In New York raw sugar futures settled firmer with the most-active March contract piercing resistance at 10.83 cents/lb and closing just under the day's high. The move was purely technical and given bearish fundamentals the market seems to be overbought. Hence, a downward correction would not come as a surprise.

RUSSIA - According to the Foreign Trade Ministry no new supply contracts are planned with Cuba. Under the existing protocol Russia is to receive 1.5 million tonnes of raw sugar in 1996/97, with the amount rising to 1.75 million tonnes in 1998, paying for it with crude oil. The Ministry also said there were no plans to sign a separate, similar deal between Cuba and the government of Russia's republic of Tatarstan.
Tatarstan officials said earlier this year they were seeking to buy 500,000 tonnes of raw sugar over an unspecified period in exchange for oil and spare parts for Russian-made heavy trucks.

OMAN - Oman has allocated land in the Mina Qaboos port for a sugar refinery with a capacity of 360,000 tonnes a year, a Reuters report said. Total investment is put at $70 million. 40 per cent of the National Sugar Refinery (NSR) will be floated on the Muscat stock exchange once the company has completed its formation, probably in February. Sixty per cent of the funds are already committed by the original founders.

The plant, expected to come on stream in late 1998, will compete in the region with Al Khaleej refinery in Dubai, which aims at an annual capacity of 720,000 tonnes, and a 500,000- tonne refinery in Saudi Arabia, which is due to start production in early 1997. EU exports will be hardest hit by the new refineries.

CZECH REPUBLIC - Sugar exports in October 1996 amounted to 3,439 tonnes, raw value, slightly up on last year's 3,218 tonnes. This brought cumulative exports in the first two months of 1996/97 (September/October) up 6,022 tonnes against 5,187 tonnes in the like period the previous year.

Total exports in 1995/96 amounted to 27,684 tonnes against 35,029 tonnes in 1994/95 and 168,648 tonnes in 1993/94. Sugar imports in September/October 1996 reached 4,541 tonnes, up from 1,465 tonnes in 1995. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 21,013 tonnes against 10,989 tonnes in 1994/95.

The European Union awarded 40,500 tonnes of white sugar at a maximum refund of ECU 46.316 per 100 kg at its weekly tender on Wednesday. Cumulative awards so far made under the 1996/97 series of tenders for the period up to December 18 reached 1,254,000 tonnes, which compares to 1,364,775 tonnes last year.
